minutes.headline: Commission denied a wetlands compliance certificate for 564 Page Street over missing restoration plantings
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission worked through a full docket of wetlands hearings (Sunset Lane, Massachusetts Ave x2, Howard Street, Electric Ave, Sandy Cove Road), continuing most to April 16th, and approved a de minimis plan change at a Massachusetts Ave. project with erosion-control follow-up. The most contested item was a certificate of compliance for 564 Page Street, where the commission found the required wetland restoration plantings had not survived as approved and voted to deny the certificate pending a wetland scientist's letter. The chair also approved two small fund expenditures (a native-plant purchase and a trail-work purchase order) and announced she will step down as chair at month's end.

what_happened.line: The commission voted 7-0 to deny a certificate of compliance for 564 Page Street after finding required wetland restoration plantings had not survived.
A commissioner will obtain a wetland scientist's letter confirming the originally-approved plantings are alive before the site can resubmit for compliance.
The commission approved a driveway/house project on Massachusetts Ave. after striking a documentation condition, and a 7-Eleven project as a minor change with erosion-control follow-up required.
Four other pending wetlands matters (Sunset Lane, Howard Street, Electric Ave., Sandy Cove Road) were continued to April 16th.
The chair announced she will resign the chair role at month's end, with chair and vice-chair nominations to be taken up April 16th.

why_it_matters: The Page Street decision means the property remains out of compliance with its wetlands permit until a scientist documents that the required plantings are established, affecting when the owner can close out the project.
Several other wetlands filings across town (driveways, a new house, erosion violations) remain open and will be taken up April 16th, which affects abutters and applicants waiting on those decisions.
Leadership of the commission is changing at the end of the month, which residents watching wetlands or conservation-fund matters may want to follow.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the outcome of nearly every vote and on the substance of most decisions, but the official minutes carry roll-call detail (individual abstentions/NA votes) that our summary collapses into a bare "passed," while our transcript mis-hears several names, one address, and one dollar figure by two decimal places. The one thing a reader should check first: the two records name different people as having agreed to follow up with NHESP on the Proctor project (Greg Roy vs. Chair Wilson), and they disagree on both the vote count and the funding source for the pollinator-habitat invoice.
